formation.title: The Restoration of the Manden Empire
formation.text:
The fragments of the great empire founded by Sundiata Keita have been gathered once more under a single banner. From the banks of the Niger to the edges of the Sahara, the Manden people are united again. The Gbara, the great assembly of clan chiefs, convenes at Kangaba to decide the direction of the restored empire.

Will we follow in the footsteps of Mansa Musa, whose golden pilgrimage dazzled the courts of Cairo and Mecca, making Mali the wealthiest realm in the known world? Or shall we heed the legacy of Sundiata the Lion King, whose warriors carved an empire from the savannah, and build our strength upon the might of the ton-tigui and the fearsome farari cavalry?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let gold speak louder than swords.

modifiers.name: Golden Throne of Niani
modifiers.text: The wealth of the Manden Empire flows through our markets like the waters of the Niger. Gold dust and salt fill our coffers, and the name of our Mansa is spoken with reverence from Timbuktu to Cairo.

options.text: The empire was won by warriors, and warriors shall keep it.

modifiers.name: Mandate of the Gbara
modifiers.text: The Great Assembly has spoken. The ton-tigui stand ready, the farari corps ride at our command, and the sixteen quiver-masters pledge their loyalty. The empire shall be held by the strength of Manden arms.

advances.name: Griot Oral Tradition
advances.text: The griots, jali in Manden, are the keepers of history, genealogy, and law. Through song and recitation, they preserve the Epic of Sundiata and the deeds of the Mansaya.

advances.name: Niani Trade Tradition
advances.text: The capital at Niani sits at the crossroads of the Niger trade routes, where goods from the forest, savannah, and desert converge in bustling markets.

advances.name: Manden Clan Governance
advances.text: The Manden political system rests on the federation of clans established by the Kouroukan Fouga, with the Gbara assembly providing counsel and consensus.

advances.name: Islam of the Mansa
advances.text: The Mansaya embraced Islam early, blending it with Manden traditions to create a distinctive West African Islamic civilization.

advances.name: Timbuktu Manuscripts
advances.text: The great libraries and madrasas of Timbuktu house hundreds of thousands of manuscripts on jurisprudence, astronomy, and history, an intellectual treasure of the Islamic world.

event.title: The Manuscripts of Timbuktu
event.text:
In the madrasas of Timbuktu, a remarkable flowering of scholarship has taken root. The scholars of Sankore have assembled a vast collection of manuscripts, texts on Islamic jurisprudence, astronomy, mathematics, medicine, and the histories of the Sahel. Scholars travel from as far as Fez and Cairo to study alongside our ulama, and the Timbuktu Manuscripts are becoming known as one of the great intellectual treasures of the Islamic world.

These manuscripts represent an immense wealth, both intellectual and material. Shall we invest in preserving and expanding this scholarly tradition, or leverage Timbuktu's fame to attract more traders and commerce to our markets?

options.text: Knowledge is the truest wealth. Preserve the manuscripts.

modifiers.name: Keepers of Timbuktu
modifiers.text: The libraries of Timbuktu hold the wisdom of ages, manuscripts on jurisprudence, astronomy, medicine, and history fill the shelves of Sankore. We are the guardians of this knowledge.

options.text: Let Timbuktu's fame fill our markets with merchants.

modifiers.name: Trade of Timbuktu
modifiers.text: Timbuktu stands at the crossroads of the world. Caravans from the Sahara meet river merchants from the Niger, and the goods of three continents change hands in our markets.

advances.name: Trans-Saharan Caravans
advances.text: Vast caravans of a thousand camels cross the desert, carrying salt south and gold north. Mali sits at the heart of this commerce.

event.title: The Great Caravans of the Sahara
event.text:
The trans-Saharan trade routes that have enriched our empire for generations continue to thrive. Vast caravans of a thousand camels and more cross the burning desert, guided by Berber navigators who read the stars as sailors read the sea. At Taghaza, great slabs of salt are cut from the earth and loaded onto camels for the long journey south. At Bure and Bambuk, gold dust is weighed and exchanged for the salt that is worth its weight in the precious metal.

Our empire sits astride these routes like a spider at the center of its web. Every caravan that passes through our territory pays tribute to the Mansa, and the wealth of nations flows through Manden hands.

options.text: We are the lords of the caravan roads.

modifiers.name: Lords of the Caravan
modifiers.text: The great caravans of a thousand camels cross the burning sands at our command. Salt from Taghaza, gold from Bure, kola from the forest, all pass through Manden territory and fill Manden purses.

advances.name: Hajj of the Mansa
advances.text: Mansa Musa's legendary pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 astounded the courts of Egypt and Arabia with its display of wealth, establishing Mali's reputation across the known world.

advances.name: Djinguereber Mosque
advances.text: Commissioned by Mansa Musa and designed by the Andalusian architect Abu Es Haq es Saheli, this great mosque defines the Sudano-Sahelian architectural tradition.

event.title: The Great Mosque of Djinguereber
event.text:
The Djinguereber Mosque, commissioned by Mansa Musa himself and designed by the Andalusian architect Abu Es Haq es Saheli, stands as the crown jewel of Sudano-Sahelian architecture. Built of banco, sun-dried mud brick reinforced with palm wood, the mosque towers over Timbuktu, its three inner courts, two minarets, and prayer halls serving as both a house of worship and a center of learning.

The mosque has become a model for Islamic architecture throughout West Africa. Its distinctive style, organic, monumental, and perfectly adapted to the Sahel climate, represents the unique synthesis of Manden creativity and Islamic devotion that defines our civilization.

options.text: A monument worthy of the Mansa's glory.

advances.name: Wangara Gold Trade
advances.text: The Wangara merchant network controls the gold fields of Bure and Bambuk through a system of silent trade, making Mali the source of much of the world's gold.

advances.name: Saharan Musket Trade
advances.text: Firearms acquired through trans-Saharan trade with North African states begin to transform Manden warfare, supplementing traditional bow and spear tactics.

advances.name: Niger River Fleet
advances.text: War canoes and trading vessels ply the Niger River, the lifeline of the empire, carrying goods and warriors between the great trading cities.

advances.name: Manden Charter Reforms
advances.text: The principles of the Kouroukan Fouga, consensus governance, craft guild autonomy, and social mobility, are adapted to meet the challenges of a new era.

event.title: Reforms of the Manden Charter
event.text:
The Kouroukan Fouga, the great charter proclaimed at Kurukan Fuga after Sundiata's victory at the Battle of Krina, has served as the constitutional foundation of our empire since its founding. Its forty-four edicts established the federation of Mandinka clans, codified property rights, mandated environmental protections, and guaranteed individual freedoms, including the abolition of slavery among the Manden.

Now a new generation of leaders seeks to adapt these ancient principles to the challenges of a changing world. The charter's emphasis on consensus governance through the Gbara assembly, its recognition of craft guild autonomy, and its provisions for social mobility offer a framework for a more modern administration.

options.text: The wisdom of the founders endures.

advances.name: Gold Dust Economy
advances.text: Gold dust serves as currency throughout the empire, weighed in standardized measures. The gold markets of Niani and Timbuktu set prices that ripple across Africa and beyond.

advances.name: Sankore Scholars
advances.text: The scholars of the Sankore Madrasa represent the intellectual pinnacle of West African Islam, producing works on Maliki jurisprudence that are studied from the Sahel to the Maghreb.

advances.name: Ton-Jon Cavalry
advances.text: The ton-jon, originally former slaves granted warrior status, evolved into a professional cavalry force serving the Mansa as a loyal military instrument beyond clan politics.

advances.name: Mande Cloth Weaving
advances.text:
The bogolan, mud cloth, tradition and strip-woven textiles of the Mande people are both artistically distinctive and commercially valuable throughout West Africa.

Available in: Sahel Caravanserai

advances.name: Maliki Jurisprudence
advances.text: The Maliki school of Islamic law, dominant in the Sahel, provides a comprehensive legal framework that governs trade, inheritance, and social relations across the empire.

advances.name: Provincial Farimba
advances.text: The farima, provincial governors drawn from the warrior aristocracy, administer the far-flung provinces of the empire, collecting tribute and maintaining order on behalf of the Mansa.

advances.name: Kola Trade Routes
advances.text: Kola nuts from the southern forests are a prized stimulant throughout the Islamic world. Controlling these trade routes adds another dimension to Mali's commercial dominance.

advances.name: Firearms Adoption
advances.text: Firearms acquired through trans-Saharan trade and local manufacture begin to transform the composition of Manden armies, creating a new class of musket-armed infantry.

advances.name: Tata Fortifications
advances.text: The tata, fortified compounds of sun-dried brick, protect Manden settlements from raids. Their thick walls and defensive towers are adapted to the Sahel environment.

advances.name: Imperial Centralization
advances.text: Administrative reforms strengthen the Mansa's authority over the provinces, reducing the autonomy of local chiefs and creating a more unified imperial bureaucracy.

advances.name: Niger Trade Network
advances.text: The Niger River serves as a commercial highway linking the empire's major cities. Control of riverine trade complements the overland caravan routes.

advances.name: Mande Diaspora
advances.text: Mande-speaking traders, craftsmen, and scholars have established communities throughout West Africa, spreading language, culture, and commerce far beyond the empire's borders.

advances.name: Sofa Military Reform
advances.text: The sofa warrior tradition is modernized with European-influenced drill and organization, creating a disciplined professional infantry force for the new age.

advances.name: Maktab Education
advances.text: Building on the madrasa tradition, a network of maktab schools extends literacy and learning beyond the scholarly elite to a broader segment of society.

advances.name: Groundnut Economy
advances.text: The cultivation and export of groundnuts transforms the agricultural economy, providing a cash crop that integrates Mali into global commodity markets.

advances.name: Modern Governance
advances.text: Modern administrative methods are adopted to govern the empire, blending Manden traditions of consensus rule with bureaucratic efficiency.

advances.name: Epic Tradition
advances.text: The oral traditions of the griots, the Epic of Sundiata, the chronicles of the Mansaya, are a living cultural heritage that defines Manden identity across the centuries.

destiny.name: The Destiny of Manden
destiny.text: The restored empire stands ready to forge its path. Whether through gold or iron, the Mansa's will shall shape the future of the Sahel.

event.title: The Destiny of Manden
event.text: The empire is restored, but our work has only begun. The Gbara convenes to declare the Mansa's vision for the future of Manden. The path we choose now will echo through the ages.

options.text: Let the Mansa's will be done.

destiny.name: Crossroads of the Sahara
destiny.text: Timbuktu and Djenne, the twin jewels of the Niger Bend, are held for the Mansa by vassals. Place them under the Mansa's own governors and build them up, so that caravans from the desert and river merchants from the south meet in cities that are truly ours.

conditions.text: Timbuktu is ours and has reached a development of 13
Djenne is ours and has reached a development of 15

event.title: Crossroads of the Sahara
event.text: Timbuktu and Djenne are ours. The Niger Bend, that great crescent where the river turns south through the desert's edge, now lies entirely under Manden control. Caravans arriving from the north find Manden tax collectors waiting at every gate, and the scholars of Sankore bow to a Manden patron.

options.text: The river bend answers to the Mansa alone.

destiny.name: Salt and Gold
destiny.text: Take the salt mines of Taghaza from the vassals who hold them into the Mansa's own hand, and build a salt depot or a gold dust market at Timbuktu, where the salt of the north is sold for the gold of the south.

conditions.text: Timbuktu is ours and a Salt Depot or a Gold Dust Market stands there

event.title: Masters of Salt and Gold
event.text:
The salt mines of Taghaza are ours, completing our grip on the two commodities that drive the trans-Saharan trade. Salt from the north, gold from the south, both now pass through Manden hands. The Mansa's market at Timbuktu weighs every slab that comes down from the desert and every measure of gold that comes up from the south, and his treasury overflows.

Shall we invest this wealth in monopolizing the salt trade itself, or in patronizing the scholars and institutions that make Timbuktu the intellectual capital of Africa?

modifiers.name: Salt Monopoly of the Mansa
modifiers.text: The Mansa controls the salt trade from mine to market, setting prices that enrich the treasury and fund the empire's ambitions.

modifiers.name: Patronage of Timbuktu
modifiers.text: The Mansa's generous patronage of Timbuktu's scholars and madrasas has made the city a beacon of learning that draws the finest minds from across the Islamic world.

destiny.name: Empire of Gold
destiny.text: Complete the golden chain from Sijilmasa in the north to the gold fields of the south, and make Niani a capital worthy of it. Let the wealth of Manden be spoken of from Marrakech to Cairo.

conditions.text: Own Sijilmasa, or a subject owns it
Niani is ours and has reached a development of 36

event.title: Empire of Gold
event.text:
From Sijilmasa in the Maghreb to the gold fields of the south, the entire golden chain lies under Manden control. No empire in Africa, perhaps none in the world, commands such wealth. The name of the Mansa is spoken with awe in the courts of Europe, the palaces of Cairo, and the bazaars of Baghdad.

Will we leverage this golden empire to dominate through diplomacy and annexation, or invest in building a lasting cultural legacy that will define West Africa for centuries?

options.text: Let gold speak in every court.

modifiers.name: The Gold Emperor
modifiers.text: The Mansa's wealth and diplomatic reach are without parallel. Gold buys allies, vassals, and influence across the known world.

options.text: Build a legacy that outlasts gold.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Mansa
modifiers.text: The Mansa has chosen to invest in a legacy beyond conquest, a civilization of learning, art, and culture that will define West Africa for centuries.

destiny.name: March on Gao
destiny.text: The Songhai city of Gao has long rivaled Manden power on the Niger. Its princes pay tribute and wait for their hour. Rule Gao directly and secure the eastern frontier.

event.title: March on Gao
event.text: The Songhai capital of Gao has fallen to Manden arms. For generations, the Songhai competed with Mali for dominance of the Niger, raiding our eastern provinces and defying the Mansa's authority. That era is over. The eastern frontier is secured, and the road to further conquest lies open.

options.text: Gao bows to the Lion King's heirs.

destiny.name: The Hausa Campaigns
destiny.text: The wealthy city-states of Hausaland, Kano and Katsina, control the trade routes east to Bornu and beyond. Conquer them, and hold half of Katsina's country directly, to extend Manden hegemony across the entire Sahel.

conditions.text: Own Kano, or a subject owns it
Own Katsina, or a subject owns it
At least half of the northern Hausa lands are ours

event.title: The Hausa Campaigns
event.text:
Our armies have swept through Hausaland, bringing the great city-states of Kano and Katsina under the Mansa's banner. These ancient trading centers, with their connections to Bornu, Egypt, and the distant east, now pay tribute to Manden.

Shall we use this momentum to reform our cavalry and press further conquests, or extract systematic tribute to fund a professional standing army?

options.text: Reform the cavalry for further campaigns.

modifiers.name: Savanna Riders
modifiers.text: The reformed Manden cavalry sweeps across the open savanna with devastating speed, recruiting and training warriors from conquered lands.

options.text: Extract tribute and build a standing army.

modifiers.name: Tribute of Hausaland
modifiers.text: The systematic extraction of tribute from the wealthy Hausa city-states funds a professional army and provides mercenary allies.

destiny.name: Lord of the Gold Coast
destiny.text: The Akan goldfields around Kumasi and Bono Manso are the source of the gold that made Mali legendary. Seize these lands, hold half of the Akan country directly, and control the wealth at its very source.

conditions.text: Own Kumasi, or a subject owns it
Own Bono Manso, or a subject owns it
At least half of the Akan lands are ours

event.title: Lord of the Gold Coast
event.text:
Kumasi and the Akan goldfields are ours. We have achieved what no Mansa before us dared, controlling not merely the trade in gold, but the mines themselves. The empire of Sundiata has been surpassed. From the salt flats of the Sahara to the forests of the Gold Coast, the Mansa's writ runs unchallenged.

Shall we use this unrivaled power for further military dominion, or consolidate our vast conquests into a lasting Pax Mandinka?

options.text: The sword of Sundiata knows no rest.

modifiers.name: Sword of Sundiata
modifiers.text: The military might of the Mansa is absolute. No fortress can withstand the combined arms of Manden infantry, cavalry, and siege warfare.

options.text: Forge a lasting peace across our domains.

modifiers.name: Pax Mandinka
modifiers.text: The Mansa's peace stretches across the Sahel and beyond. War-weary lands recover under stable Manden governance, and disease and devastation recede.

units.name: Saharan Musketeer
units.text: Infantry armed with muskets acquired through trans-Saharan trade, combining traditional Manden tactical discipline with firearm technology.

units.name: Ton-Jon Horseman
units.text: Professional cavalry warriors drawn from the ton-jon warrior class, famed for their speed, ferocity in raids, and absolute loyalty to the Mansa.

units.name: Mande Arquebusier
units.text: Manden infantry trained in the use of arquebuses, representing the maturation of firearms warfare in the Sahel.

units.name: Niger War Canoe
units.text: Sturdy canoes built for river warfare and trade on the Niger, crewed by experienced rivermen who know every bend and sandbar of the great river.

units.name: Reformed Sofa
units.text: The sofa warrior tradition reformed with modern drill and discipline, creating a professional infantry force that carries forward the martial legacy of old Mali.

buildings.name: Griot Pavilion
buildings.text: A gathering place where griots, the hereditary keepers of oral history, perform the epics and genealogies that bind Manden society together.

buildings.name: Sahel Caravanserai
buildings.text: A fortified rest stop along the trans-Saharan trade routes, providing shelter, water, and markets for the great caravans crossing the desert.

buildings.name: Manuscript Library
buildings.text: The house library of a scholar family, after those of Timbuktu. Books bought from the caravans of the north are copied here by paid scribes, lent to students, and handed down as the family's wealth. Law, grammar, astronomy and medicine are read in its court.

buildings.name: Salt Depot
buildings.text: A warehouse and market for the salt trade, the great slabs of rock salt from Taghaza are stored, divided, and sold to merchants heading south.

buildings.name: Sudano-Sahelian Mosque
buildings.text: A monumental mosque built in the distinctive banco mud-brick style of the Sahel, serving as both a center of worship and a seat of learning.

buildings.name: Gold Dust Market
buildings.text: A specialized market where gold dust is weighed, valued, and traded. The gold markets of Mali set prices that influence commerce across Africa and the Mediterranean.

buildings.name: Tata Fortress
buildings.text: A fortified compound of sun-dried brick with defensive towers, adapted to the Sahel landscape. The tata tradition protects settlements from raids and invasions.

buildings.name: Maktab School
buildings.text: A school providing basic literacy and Quranic education to the broader population, extending the madrasa tradition beyond the scholarly elite.

buildings.name: Somono Landing
buildings.text: A river station of the Somono, the boatmen of the Niger. In return for their privileges the ruler's grain, salt, soldiers and orders are carried along the river in their sewn canoes.

buildings.name: House of Gold
buildings.text: A grand treasury and trade palace where the wealth of the trans-Saharan trade is weighed, stored, and redistributed. The finest merchants and bankers in West Africa conduct their business beneath its golden domes.

buildings.name: Sundiata's Hall
buildings.text: A fortified palace-fortress honoring the empire's founder, where the Mansa holds court with his war chiefs and the greatest warriors of the empire are honored.

list.name: Gbara Assembly
list.text: The great council instituted by the Kurukan Fuga charter of 1236, where some thirty seats represented the Mandinka clan federation: sixteen ton-tigi warrior lineages, four mori-kanda-lolou guardians of the faith for Islamic counsel, four niamakala caste clans for craft-corporate matters, and four djeli clans as masters of speech and historical record. The Gbara advised the Mansa, ratified successions, and embodied the federal contract that bound the twelve vassal kingdoms to Niani. Its consensus was an asset to legitimacy and a brake on the throne in equal measure.

list.name: Dyamana Provincial Government
list.text: Mali was a federation of twelve component kingdoms under the Mansa, each ruled by a dyamani-tigui (province master) confirmed by the imperial court but chosen by local custom: election, inheritance, or rotation among recognized lineages. Conquered territories outside the Manden core were placed under a farba military governor appointed directly by the Mansa, who collected tribute and customs and held local judicial authority. The dual structure of consensual federalism for the heartland and direct rule for the periphery distinguished the Mali Empire from its tributary Songhai successor.

list.name: Sankore Madrasa Complex
list.text: By the 14th century Timbuktu housed three great congregational madrasas: the Djinguereber, built in 1327 under Mansa Musa to a design by the Andalusian Es-Saheli; the Sidi Yahya, founded around 1440; and the older Sankore mosque, which matured into a centre for Maliki jurisprudence, mathematics, astronomy, and grammar. At its height the complex hosted some twenty-five thousand students and a class of black-robed jurists whose fatawa were sought from Cairo to Marrakech. The library culture they sustained survived the Moroccan conquest of 1591 in private hands, scattered into the desert against the day of return.

list.name: Wangara Trading Diaspora
list.text: The long-distance Muslim merchants known as Wangara in the Sahel and Dyula in the southern forests, drawn from Soninke and Mandinka stock and bound by a shared Maliki rite. From the fourteenth century the Wangara organized the prospecting and transport of gold from Bambuk, Bure, and the Akan country, the salt caravans from Taghaza, the cola nut exchange from Kong, and the Saharan paper-and-book trade. Their decentralized colony-network of merchant quarters in non-Muslim trading towns (Begho, Kong, Bobo-Dioulasso, Bonduku) extended Manden commercial reach far beyond the formal political frontier of the empire.

list.name: Niamakala Caste Corporations
list.text: The endogamous artisan castes formalized in the Kurukan Fuga of 1236: the numu blacksmiths who alone could work iron, the garanke leatherworkers, the djeli griot-bards who tutored princes and chronicled the empire, and the fune Islamic praise-singers. Each clan held a hereditary monopoly on its craft and a recognized place at the Mansa's court. Strict endogamy and ritual taboo separated the niamakala from the freeborn horon, but in return the castes wielded a corporate authority over their trades that no royal edict could lightly overturn: the institutional spine of Manden craft and memory.

list.name: Ton-tigi Cavalry Order
list.text: The carriers of the quiver, the sixteen warrior lineages who at the Kurukan Fuga were granted the right to bear arms in the Mansa's name. Mounted on Sahelian horses imported through the trans-Saharan trade and equipped with imported chainmail and the lance, the farari (brave men) of the ton-tigi were the empire's striking force and the personal retinue of the Mansa on campaign. Their hereditary privileges, including the right to retain captives as dyon royal slaves, made them the indispensable but fractious aristocratic underlay of Manden military power, and, eventually, its undoing.
